leading_positions.synthesis: Both supporters prefer optical-lattice quantum simulation of Hubbard physics as a mature, quantitatively confirmed programme, and Johansson moved to it from B002 in round 1. They differ on the trio: Johansson names Bloch, Greiner and Esslinger, while Lindroth names Bloch, Greiner and Zoller to keep the theory proposal. Kroll also favours the experimental trio in his reasoning, but his preferred configuration is B024, so he is not counted here. Both acknowledge that any three of the five credited names leaves out a strong contributor, that Zoller and Cirac also appear in B006, and that the doped Hubbard payoff is still pending.

Both supporters prefer MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero and Bistritzer for the magic-angle prediction and the observation of correlated insulating and superconducting states; Mehlig moved to B021 from B009 in round 1. They agree that the central discovery is reproduced by many groups and that the unresolved pairing mechanism is a follow-up question. They also acknowledge that Cao and the parallel experimental groups cannot be named. Danielsson and Olsson rank it highly but regard it as young, and Danielsson would accept a two-name version.

Both prefer Katori and Ye for optical lattice clocks as the cleanest, most independently reproduced measurement result on the list. Kroll treats it as a stand-alone prize; Pearce uses it as the second part of a two-part configuration with B052. Shared reservations are proximity to the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, and that the output so far is tighter limits and a pending redefinition of the second, not a new fact about nature. Allocation between Katori's conception and Ye's precision work, and priority questions, are not yet resolved.

Danielsson prefers Costa, Frontera and Kulkarni for the discovery of gamma-ray burst afterglows and their cosmological origin, as a decisive observation with about three decades of confirmation. Pearce ranks it second and keeps it as his first alternative. The three names use the whole three-person budget, and the optical and redshift credit (van Paradijs, Groot and others) is open to challenge.

Pearce alone proposes a two-part prize pairing a one-name IceCube neutrino-astronomy part (Halzen) with the lattice-clock part (Katori, Ye), giving three laureates. The parts have no thematic unity. Danielsson ranked B052 second, but Kroll, Lindroth and Olsson raised attribution concerns about a Halzen-only prize, and Pearce himself names that as the weakest point.

Olsson alone prefers Moodera, Miyazaki and Parkin for room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance, as a finished and verified discovery with real device consequences. Eriksson ranked it fourth but doubts the attribution for the MgO step and the closeness to the 2007 GMR prize; Olsson would anchor the citation on the 1995 discovery and wants the priority question with Yuasa checked.

areas_of_agreement: No candidate is the preferred configuration of more than two members; the eight files show four configurations with two explicit supporters or fewer each (B020, B021, B024, plus the Pearce two-part B052+B024), and singles for B025 and B005.

B024 is treated as scientifically strong and well confirmed across independent laboratories by nearly every member who discusses it (Kroll, Lindroth, Johansson, Eriksson, Danielsson, Olsson, Mehlig, Pearce); it appears as a first alternative for Eriksson, Johansson and Lindroth and as a second alternative for Danielsson and Olsson.
Members agree that the main obstacle to many candidates is the three-person limit, since B020, B021, B025 and B052 each leave out contributors with a real claim.
Danielsson, Pearce and Olsson all note that the one-name credit for IceCube (B052) is problematic given the size of the collaboration; no member argues the credit is adequate as supplied.
Several members accept the central B021 finding as established while regarding the pairing mechanism as an open follow-up question (Eriksson, Mehlig, Danielsson, Olsson).
scientific_disputes: Discovery about nature versus precision measurement: Danielsson, Eriksson, Mehlig and Olsson argue that clocks have so far yielded limits and not a new phenomenon, whereas Kroll and Pearce argue that a new measurement capability is itself the achievement.

Whether quantum simulation (B020) has produced a decisive result or is a still-maturing programme whose headline payoff, the doped Hubbard model, is not yet in hand (Eriksson, Johansson, Kroll, Olsson, Mehlig raise this; Lindroth answers that the Mott transition and single-site observation were themselves the discovery).

Whether the unresolved superconducting pairing mechanism in twisted bilayer graphene weakens the case for B021 (Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson, Pearce, Danielsson) or is a follow-up that does not affect the discovery (Eriksson, Mehlig).
Whether DMFT (B019) and Berry and Aharonov-Bohm phases (B047) are discoveries or method and concept prizes; they are alternatives only for Mehlig and Eriksson, and are not preferred by anyone.
attribution_disputes: B020: Lindroth proposes Bloch, Greiner and Zoller, whereas Johansson, Kroll and Pearce propose Bloch, Greiner and Esslinger; Cirac and Zoller also appear under B006, and Jaksch and Hansch are outside the credited list.
B021: Danielsson would drop Bistritzer for a pair (MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero), Eriksson and Mehlig keep all three; Cao and the parallel Dean, Yacoby and Young groups cannot be named.
B052: only Halzen is credited, although the 2013 detection and the source associations rest on a large collaboration of instrument builders and analysis leaders not on the list.

B025: the BeppoSAX localisation credit (Costa, Frontera) and the optical afterglow and redshift credit (Kulkarni; van Paradijs deceased; Groot and others) are separable, and three names may not represent both.
B024: Katori's conception and first demonstration versus Ye's systematics work, and priority claims by other groups, have not been independently verified by any member.
B005: Parkin's inclusion rests on the later MgO step, in parallel with Yuasa and Djayaprawira, while the theory of Butler and Mathon lies outside the credited names.
maturity_disputes: B021 is about eight years old; Eriksson and Mehlig regard broad replication as sufficient, while Danielsson, Olsson and Kroll would prefer waiting, and Olsson calls it slightly early.
B052 has a solid diffuse flux, but source identification (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068, Galactic plane) remains at moderate significance (Danielsson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson, Pearce).
B020 and B024 each have about two decades of independent confirmation, but the pending redefinition of the second (B024) and the doped Hubbard question (B020) are cited as unfinished outcomes.
B025 is regarded as fully mature by Danielsson, who contrasts it with IceCube and with B021.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson-Goran directs WACQT at Chalmers and knows the B002 candidates (Blais, Wallraff, Schoelkopf, Girvin); she states she should recuse from a final decision on B002 and be cautious on B026 and B022. B002 is no longer her preferred configuration.

Kroll-Stefan spent a year of his PhD in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder and Jun Ye is a later JILA colleague of Hall; he reports no collaboration, shared funding or institutional tie to Katori or Ye. His own field is close to B024, B020, B006, B002 and B043.

Pearce-Mark (Chair) works in PAMELA, Fermi-LAT and XL-Calibur; he reports no tie to IceCube, the clock candidates or their credited names, but his astroparticle background is close to B052 and B025 and he asks colleagues to weigh his views there accordingly.

Lindroth-Eva notes that atomic physics is close to several shortlisted entries and has no known tie to the credited names, and Eriksson-Olle notes scientific proximity to B019 and B005; neither reports a formal conflict.
Mehlig-Bernhard and Olsson-Eva note Chalmers colleagues without any specific collaboration, and Danielsson-Ulf reports no connection.
questions_for_round2: B052: can the committee settle a credible set of names for IceCube within the three-person limit, and if a one-name Halzen prize is not defensible, does the B052 plus B024 configuration have to be dropped?

B024: does a lattice-clock citation anchored on the magic-wavelength lattice and 10^-18 uncertainty distinguish it enough from the 2005 and 2012 prizes, and is the Katori-Ye split robust against priority claims (Kroll to answer)?

B020: if the committee chose this, is the discovery the Jaksch-Zoller proposal plus the Mott observation (Bloch, Greiner, Zoller) or the experimental realisation including fermionic and single-site work (Bloch, Greiner, Esslinger), and how should Zoller's and Cirac's presence in B006 be handled?
B021: can members who regard the pairing question as open say whether a 2026 award is acceptable, and is the three-name or the two-name version (without Bistritzer) preferable?
Can any two-part or single-part configuration command support from members who ranked neither of its parts first, given that no ballot is the preferred configuration of more than two members?
B025 and B005: would Danielsson and Olsson say what additional attribution evidence (optical afterglow credit; Parkin versus Yuasa on MgO tunnelling) would let their single-supporter positions move?
summary.chair_observation: The first-round files show a dispersed committee: six distinct preferred configurations among eight members, with B020, B021 and B024 each drawing two explicit supporters and none more. The differences are less about the quality of the science than about whether a prize should reward a discovery about nature or a new measurement capability, how much weight to give maturity, and who can be named under the three-person limit. Each leading candidate carries a specific unresolved attribution point, which round 2 should address before ballots are compared.
